note: Every fact this page renders resolves to one of these entries. 'official-doc' and 'official-pdf' are Kalshi-published pages or documents; 'official-api' is a verbatim response from a Kalshi host, with the request that produced it. No third-party source is used for any number, field name or endpoint.

facts.claim: Demo REST Trade API recommended base URL is https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2; https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 is also supported.
Demo WebSocket URL is wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2; wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2 is also supported.
The OpenAPI document lists exactly four servers: external-api.kalshi.com, api.elections.kalshi.com, external-api.demo.kalshi.co and demo-api.kalshi.co, all under /trade-api/v2.

GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook needs no authentication, returns orderbook_fp.yes_dollars and orderbook_fp.no_dollars, each a list of [price_dollars, count_fp] strings sorted ascending, best bid last, bids only; the implied YES ask is $1.00 minus the highest NO bid.
An empty book and a ticker that matches no market both return HTTP 200 with empty arrays, so emptiness must never be read as a price of zero.

Candlesticks: GET /series/{series_ticker}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks with required start_ts and end_ts (Unix seconds) and period_interval in {1, 60, 1440} minutes; each candle has end_period_ts, yes_bid/yes_ask/price OHLC in *_dollars and volume_fp.
GET /markets accepts limit up to 1000 (default 100) with a cursor; GET /events accepts limit up to 200 (default 200) with a cursor.

Market status enum is initialized, inactive, active, closed, determined, disputed, amended, finalized; the status= filter maps unopened->initialized, open->active, paused->inactive, closed->past close_time not finalized, settled->finalized.
result is one of 'yes', 'no', 'scalar' or the empty string, and settlement_ts / settlement_value_dollars are filled only after determination.

WebSocket connections require API-key authentication during the handshake; even public market-data channels (ticker, trade, market_lifecycle_v2) run over an authenticated session. A rejected handshake returns an HTTP error instead of upgrading.
The ticker channel message carries price_dollars, yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, yes_bid_size_fp, yes_ask_size_fp, volume_fp, open_interest_fp, dollar_volume and ts_ms.
Trading fee = round up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) for taker fills; maker fee = round up(M x 0.0175 x C x P x (1-P)); there is no settlement fee. Schedule effective July 7, 2026.
Fees are six-decimal dollar amounts rounded up, with a per-order rounding accumulator; direct members' balances align to $0.0001 and non-direct to $0.01.
The demo environment uses mock funds, has credentials separate from production, and its prices and behaviour may not reflect real markets; the demo site is https://demo.kalshi.co/.
Rate limits are token buckets per tier; most requests cost 10 tokens; unauthenticated public requests are subject to separate limits and a limited request returns HTTP 429.

GET /search/tags_by_categories returns the official category-to-tag map: Crypto, Elections, Entertainment, Sports (with a Golf tag), Economics (with 'Oil and energy'), Commodities (with 'Oil & Gas'). There is no 'Culture' and no 'Gas' category.

GET /series supports category (exact, case-sensitive, matches any entry in the series' categories list) and tags filters and returns ticker, category, categories, tags and settlement_sources per series.

GET /series/{ticker} returns the same fields for one series; for KXAAAGASM it returns categories ['Economics'], tags ['Oil & Gas','Oil and energy'] and settlement source AAA (https://gasprices.aaa.com/).
GET /events?with_nested_markets=true returns each event with its markets array, so one paginated scan yields both event titles and live market quotes.
GET /markets supports a comma-separated tickers filter, which allows one cheap request to refresh the quotes of a fixed watch list.
previous_price_dollars, previous_yes_bid_dollars and previous_yes_ask_dollars are the values from a day ago, not from the previous poll; they cannot be used to detect a short-term swing.
Candlesticks for markets that settled before the historical cutoff are only available from GET /historical/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks, so an empty candlestick array is not proof of no trading.

The demo hosts echo Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the GitHub Pages origin on public reads (HTTP 200, credentials true), and the signed-order OPTIONS preflight returns 204 without listing the Kalshi signing headers among allowed request headers.
An unauthenticated WebSocket handshake to both demo hosts is rejected with HTTP 401 and body {"code":"token_authentication_failure"}.
GET /exchange/status returns exchange_active, trading_active and per-shard statuses; on 2026-11-22T07:26Z the demo exchange reported exchange_active=true and trading_active=true.

GET /portfolio/balance requires API-key auth, returns balance in cents plus balance_dollars, portfolio_value in cents and updated_ts, and has its own rate-limit bucket of 1 request per second on Basic/Advanced tiers.

GET /portfolio/positions requires API-key auth and returns market_positions[] with ticker, position_fp (positive = YES, negative = NO), market_exposure_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars, fees_paid_dollars and total_traded_dollars.

platform_limits: The page is static GitHub Pages HTML/JS. It holds no API key, so it can read public market data only, and cannot place, amend or cancel any order.

A WebSocket price stream to Kalshi requires a signed handshake (S10). A browser page cannot hold that key safely, so this page polls REST and states its polling interval rather than claiming to be a stream.
The demo exchange's prices are generated by demo participants and may not reflect production prices (S14). They are labelled as demo values everywhere on this page.
